headline: High: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces can feed pdf.js browser/file parsing, creating default-path prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks, while pdf.js ingests PDF files in a browser-based worker model. A shared workspace or copied outputs can let attacker-controlled document content influence downstream interpretation, but the pair lacks a documented direct channel, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are copied into PDF content or browser-rendered text that pdf.js later parses as trusted instructions
IF both agents share a filesystem or message queue without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata-generated text into pdf.js workflows
Add provenance labels before any handoff
Review PDFs as untrusted input before parsing
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include sensitive metadata. pdf.js only lists PDF files and has no network egress, so leakage is not from uncontrolled outbound transfer; however, a shared workspace can still expose sensitive documents or metadata across the pair in default collaboration setups.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or document repository
IF OpenMetadata stores sensitive governance or lineage data in files that pdf.js can open
mitigations: Use separate directories for metadata and PDFs
Restrict pdf.js to read-only access
Mask sensitive fields before export from OpenMetadata
Audit shared mounts for accidental cross-access
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the storage layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and can act through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP; pdf.js also supports multiple instances and runs browser-based tests. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap, but if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or repository, concurrent edits and state drift are plausible, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository, workspace, or metadata store
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or optimistic concurrency control
mitigations: Assign separate write targets
Turn on repository locking if available
Schedule non-overlapping runs
Keep pdf.js read-only in shared environments
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit lineage, governance, and trust metadata that pdf.js may render or use in browser-based tests. If pdf.js treats that output as authoritative without verification, a bad catalog entry or malformed document can cascade into incorrect downstream rendering or decisions. The pair lacks evidence of built-in verification between them, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes OpenMetadata output as authoritative input without a validation step
IF OpenMetadata metadata is used to drive browser-based tests or document rendering decisions
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require human review for high-impact metadata
Compare outputs against source PDFs before acting
Log provenance for every handoff
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and trust scoring

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata’s governance and lineage data classes can include regulated metadata, while pdf.js only processes PDF files and has no network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented here, so the compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive PDFs or metadata in a shared workflow rather than a clear policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs or metadata are routed through both agents in the same workflow
IF the deployment has a residency or retention policy that differs between catalog metadata and PDF storage
mitigations: Classify PDFs before processing
Keep regulated data out of shared test fixtures
Set retention rules for exported metadata
Review residency requirements for any shared storage
requires-engineering: document and enforce policy mappings per data class
